                                  CITY OF EASTPORT, MAINE

                                    MOTION TO INTERVENE

        Pursuant to Rule 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“FERC”) Rules of

Practice and Procedure, the City of Eastport, Maine (“City”), by and through its undersigned

counsel, Rudman Winchell, moves to intervene in the above-referenced proceeding regarding the

DeepGreen Western Passage SPV LLC (“DeepGreen”) preliminary permit application for the

proposed Subsea-Compute and Infrastructure Hub Project (“Project”). 18 C.F.R. § 385.214. By

this motion, the City seeks to ensure that the City’s interests and the interests of its citizens are

adequately represented during FERC’s evaluation of the Project. In support of its motion, the

City states the following:

                                   CONTACT INFORMATION

        Pursuant to Rule 2010 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 C.F.R. §

385.2010, all filings, orders, and correspondence regarding this proceeding should be served as

                              DESCRIPTION OF INTERVENOR

       The City is a municipal government body created under the Constitution and laws of the

State of Maine. All powers of the City are vested in the City Council, which is comprised of five

members elected by the qualified voters of the City at large, unless otherwise provided by law or

by the City Charter.

                                  THE PROPOSED PROJECT

       On February 11, 2026, and supplemented and amended on June 8, 2026, and July 30,

2026, DeepGreen filed an application pursuant to Section 4(f) of the Federal Power Act (FPA)

for a preliminary permit in order to study the feasibility of the proposed underwater data center

project. If approved, the Project would be located in the Western Passage of the Bay of Fundy in

the North Atlantic Ocean near and in the City of Eastport, Washington County, Maine. On

August 25, 2026, FERC published Notice of this Project in the Federal Register and set deadlines

for filing comments, motions to intervene, competing applications (without notices of intent), or

notices of intent to file competing applications.

       The proposed Project would consist of the following new features: (1) a 3.5-meter-high

and 24-meter-wide subsea modular universal docking cradle; (2) thirty-four 12-meter-long and

4.2-meter-diameter subsea compute pods; (3) a 1.8-meter-diameter spherical and elevated tidal



                                                                                                    2
 sensing power platform; (4) up to 16 marine hydrokinetic turbine-generator units, each rated at

300-kilowatt (kW); and (5) a 1.5-mile-long hybrid power-and-fiber subsea cable operating at

13.8 kilovolts (kV). The proposed Project would be configured as a behind-the-meter captive

generation loop without a grid connection. The Project would be situated north of the City in the

Western Passage of the Bay of Fundy, a deep tidal channel north of the City. The Project would

include a single, armored 1.5-mile hybrid power-and-fiber subsea cable, which lands at a shore-

based facility on Kendall Head, within the City’s boundaries. The Project boundary would be

restricted to 27.1 acres.

                            THE PUBLIC INTEREST REQUIRES

                                THE CITY’S INTERVENTION

        The City states the following in compliance with Rule 214(b) of the Commission’s Rules

of Practice and Procedure, 18 C.F.R. § 385.214(b):

i. 18 C.F.R. § 385.214(b)(1) Position of Movant:

        See enclosed as Exhibit A the September 22, 2026, comment of the City of Eastport City

Council. A copy of this comment has or will be submitted also as a comment, independent from

this motion. The City further reserves the right to supplement this position based on additional

anticipated submissions by DeepGreen or other interested parties.

ii. 18 C.F.R. § 385.214(b)(2) Right to Participate and Representation of an Interest Affected

by the Proceeding:

        The City has a right to seek intervention to become a party as conferred in 18 C.F.R. §

385.214(a)(3).

        In this proceeding, DeepGreen proposes a hybrid tidal-energy/data-center facility in the

Western Passage of the Bay of Fundy, which would connect to and be located adjacent to the



                                                                                                   3
 City. The proposed Project is in an area with significant economic, environmental, and cultural

significance for the City’s inhabitants. Therefore, the City has a direct and substantial interest in

this proceeding that cannot adequately be represented by any other party. Additionally, the siting

and the construction of the proposed Project would have the potential to significantly affect the

citizens and businesses of the City. Accordingly, the City has a direct and substantial interest in

and will be directly affected by the outcome of this proceeding.

       Finally, the City’s participation is in the public interest. The City seeks to intervene in the

public interest to ensure that it receives sufficient notice and is afforded the opportunity to

comment, as necessary, as more details about the Project become available.

                                          CONCLUSION

       The City has a substantial interest in this proceeding due to the fact that the Project is

proposed to be located within and adjacent to the City. The City respectfully requests that the

Commission grant the City’s Motion to Intervene in the DeepGreen Western Passage Subsea-

Compute & Infrastructure Hub Project No. 15424-000.
